# 油價回落讓美債喘息，AI債供給仍考驗買盤

## 週五反彈，仍難扭轉整週債市跌勢

油價週五回落至$100以下，帶動美債反彈，但還不足以扭轉這一週的跌勢。2年期殖利率下跌4個基點至4.33%，10年期下跌2個基點至4.69%，兩者仍比前一週五高約15個基點。布蘭特原油跌3.88%至$96.78，30年期殖利率卻幾乎不動，收在5.16%。

這次反彈主要反映通膨補償下降，而非實質借款成本降低。10年期損益兩平通膨率跌2個基點至2.26%，實質殖利率維持2.43%。美國服務業活動與新屋銷售改善，加上新關稅生效、聯準會指引不明，7月升息仍不能排除。市場在7月28至29日會議前，仍給予約35%的升息機率。

企業借款人面對的則是另一道難題：接連而來的大型AI融資，正消耗買盤承接能力。Meta資料中心的$123億債券，截至週五稍晚累積$200億訂單，僅為發行額的1.6倍，預計週一才定價。巴克萊估算也顯示，大型科技公司對美國投資級債市場的存續期間乘利差風險貢獻，已超過大型銀行。油價下跌有利公債，卻無法消除AI供給增加，以及英國、日本主權債殖利率上升帶來的資金競爭。

## 油價緩解短端壓力，實質殖利率仍高

美債在連續三個交易日由短端領跌後反彈。5年期殖利率下跌3個基點至4.43%，介於2年期的4個基點跌幅，以及30年期的1個基點跌幅之間。曲線轉陡，2s10s擴大2個基點至36個基點，2s30s擴大3個基點至83個基點。

油價是最直接的喘息來源。中東航線仍有油輪通行，調停消息也帶來局勢降溫的希望，WTI下跌3.12%至$89.31。但航運遠未恢復正常：胡塞攻擊讓威脅從荷莫茲延伸至紅海，部分船舶改道，或關閉訊號通行。布蘭特仍比一週前高9.85%、比一個月前高25.56%；WTI單週漲幅也達8.27%。

利率市場因此保留了本週大部分調整。2年期與5年期殖利率整週各上升15個基點，10年期升14個基點，30年期升10個基點；一個月累計升幅依序為17、16、19、22個基點。週五短端只收復近期政策重新定價的一部分，長端則仍背負過去一個月累積的跌幅。

抗通膨債最清楚地顯示反彈的限制。10年期實質殖利率維持2.43%，比一週前高12個基點、比一個月前高14個基點。名目10年期殖利率的跌幅，完全來自損益兩平通膨率下降2個基點；後者整週也僅上升2個基點。油價回落後，投資人願意接受較少通膨補償，卻還不願降低要求的實質報酬。

聯準會決策仍充滿變數。7月升息機率約35%，高於6月CPI降溫後的約10%，但維持利率不變仍是較可能結果。主席Kevin Warsh減少使用前瞻指引，也增加判斷難度，MOVE指數升至5月以來最高。經濟學家仍預期聯準會下一步是降息，金融市場卻押注借款成本上升。

最新美國數據未給官員急著寬鬆的理由。服務業抵銷製造業降溫，帶動企業活動以八個月來最快速度擴張，新屋銷售也增加。另一方面，涵蓋約60個經濟體、稅率10%至12.5%的進口關稅生效，取代即將到期的10%全球進口稅。影響將陸續反映在消費者價格、企業利潤或貿易流向；在需求仍有韌性時，聯準會又多了一項潛在成本衝擊需要評估。

長債受惠最少。20年期以上美債指數整週仍跌1.48%，一個月跌4.39%。政府借款與科技業資本支出，同時向保險、退休基金等長期資金爭取配置。油價大跌之際，30年期殖利率卻只下降1個基點，足見這些壓力尚未消退。

## Meta訂單簿，讓AI供給壓力有了具體價格

最新Meta專案融資，讓市場對AI借款的擔憂落到實際需求上。BlackRock旗下Sopaipilla Investor推銷$123億、2048年到期債券，用於艾爾帕索資料中心。知情人士表示，週五稍晚最終訂單達$200億，認購倍數1.6倍，遠低於今年投資級債交易約4倍的平均。預計定價日為7月27日，週五收盤時尚未完成。

定價指引約為10年期美債加287.5個基點，比同為Meta專案、2049年到期的Beignet債高約40個基點；後者7月以來本身也已擴大逾50個基點。新交易以特殊目的公司發債、逐步償還本金，並由Meta租約承諾支持，融資園區預計提供最多1吉瓦算力。BlackRock旗下Global Infrastructure Management與HPS Investment Partners合計持有專案80%，Meta持有20%。

這些保障仍未換來充裕訂單。Amazon在7月稍早發行的$250億債，也只有1.6倍認購。Meta的4月$250億融資，定價已比六個月前的$300億交易更寬，其中2046年到期券自發行後利差再擴大30個基點。相較之下，Sopaipilla並非孤例：即使租戶或發行人評等良好，大額交易不斷湧入，融資成本仍在提高。

巴克萊的指數分析進一步說明，影響不只限於單筆交易。截至7月23日，六大科技公司占美國投資級債存續期間乘利差（DTS）風險的8.6%，超過六大銀行的7.3%。大型雲端業者只占流通本金約4%，銀行則約9%，但前者較長的到期結構放大了風險貢獻。過去一年，雲端業者發債有43%超過10年期，併購相關債券為24%，其他非金融業發債為23%。

科技投資級債利差已從2026年初約76個基點，升至約89個基點。巴克萊預估，今年全球雲端業者投資級債發行約$2,850億。既有持有人除了利率風險，也面臨新券讓利帶動舊券重新定價。週五LQD跌0.03%、HYG持平、JNK跌0.01%，看似平靜，但一個月累計LQD跌2.46%，HYG與JNK各跌0.80%、0.89%，投資級債較重的存續期間負擔已反映在報酬上。

AI以外的融資，更多反映個別資產負債表問題。Victoria因資產減記及減債成本，公布全年虧損£3.263億。這也凸顯再融資背後的營運負擔：其2028年債券重整，在本週稍早獲HSBC支持後才得以推進。

Charter Communications則趁到期壓力尚未進一步升高，先整理複雜的債務結構。交換或買回要約涵蓋約$100億關係企業及Time Warner Cable債券，以及最多$97億其他子公司債務，並依參與情況，發行最多$35億、2038年及2041年到期新券。不同交換條件、償付順位與參與上限，對各券持有人影響不一，並非全面減債。

兩家受壓的歐洲借款人也在修復營運的同時安排流動性。非投資級的South East Water為未來發債取得£2億備援支持，以支應現金及£19億投資計畫。但其槓桿比率66.5%，高於55%目標，供水服務失誤又帶來£3,050萬補償方案。BayWa在舉債擴張後，負債超過€100億；先前重整已需約€13億新增銀行借款，下一步計畫還包括將最多€7億貸款改為次順位、至少€2.2億股東資金，以及出售資產。

提供私人資本的機構也在改變。私募股權對壽險公司的投資，從2009年約$230億增至約$2,500億。以評等為基礎的保險資本規範，可能使客製化私人結構比風險相近的公開債券享有較低資本要求。資金來源擴大之餘，評等品質，以及資產管理公司和保險公司的關係，也成為檢視底層貸款時不能忽略的環節。

中國的銀行面對的幾乎是相反問題：信貸需求弱，市場利率持續下降。工商銀行、招商銀行及浦發銀行海口分行，開始承作連結存款類金融機構附買回利率的貸款，不再只依賴貸款市場報價利率（LPR）。工行的CNY7,670萬貸款為期1年，連結隔夜附買回利率；浦發貸出CNY700萬，官媒報導招行金額為CNY800萬。今年3月近半數新貸款已低於LPR定價，2019年僅16%。銀行間利率與債券殖利率下降得比LPR快，改用實際交易利率，可讓貸款報價更即時反映資金成本。

## 全球主權債殖利率，未隨美債明顯回落

美國以外，主權債殖利率仍處於多年高點。彭博全球公債指數平均殖利率達3.68%，為2008年以來最高。德國10年期殖利率在2011年以來高位，英國仍高於5%，日本最長天期公債則繼續下跌。

英國10年期殖利率週五跌約4個基點至約5.04%，但整週都在5%以上，為近二十年來最長的一段。能源進口依賴，加上首相Andy Burnham支出計畫的不確定性，使財政前景更複雜。6月付息成本£118億，顯示龐大債務在高利率下的負擔。

英國央行賣債也是供給的重要一環。央行須決定10月開始的新年度，如何縮減手中剩餘£4,920億公債。當年度已出售£210億，加上到期部位，整體減少£700億；下一年度到期量將明顯縮小，債務管理局卻計畫增加長債發行。英國央行先前估計，量化緊縮已使10年期殖利率增加15至25個基點。

歐元區調查顯示的通膨壓力較溫和，但時間都早於這波油價急升。消費者1年通膨預期從3.5%降至3%，3年預期從2.9%降至2.8%。企業預估薪資增幅由2025年的3.1%，降為2026年的2.5%與2027年的2.4%，售價漲幅也低於原先預期。不過，消費者調查在6月4至29日進行，企業訪談7月1日便結束。數據能說明先前價格壓力有所緩和，還不能反映家庭與企業如何因應$100油價。

ECB週四維持利率後，官員仍保留9月升息選項。歐元區民間企業活動也升至五個月高點，削弱了以成長疲弱為由暫緩緊縮的論據。另一方面，ECB開始讓外國央行加入強化版附買回機制，預計2026年第4季起，透過五大國家央行提供；也將氣候因素擴及作為擔保品的非金融企業信貸債權，以防範轉型造成的估值損失。這些調整涉及歐元流動性取得與擔保品待遇，不是當期政策利率變動。

日本匯率與超長債同時承壓。日圓跌至163.99兌$1，為1986年11月以來最低；40年期日本公債殖利率升10個基點至4.01%，接近5月4.355%的紀錄。進口成本增加，又疊加未來減稅及國防支出的財源疑慮。

日本銀行6月把政策利率升至1%後，市場普遍預期7月31日維持不變。不過，交易價格仍計入年底前約32個基點緊縮，半數受訪經濟學家則認為下次升息在12月。若加快升息，國內殖利率可能提高、海外債券相對吸引力下降；若等待，日圓可能繼續走弱、增加進口通膨。兩種情況都使超長債投資人難以擺脫匯率、政策與財政的不確定性。

比利時也出現財政警訊。Morningstar DBRS維持AA評等，卻將展望改為負向；公共債務為GDP的107.9%，赤字5.2%、居歐元區之冠，預計2028年擴大至5.7%。聯合政府希望到2029年完成€100億財政整頓，但DBRS認為，現有政治條件下難以進行更大調整。

俄羅斯央行週五延續為期一年的降息循環，通膨壓力卻在增加。決議前政策利率為14.25%；6月經季調年化通膨升至10.6%，家庭通膨預期升至14.7%。汽油比一年前貴20%，財政部也因投標疲弱停止OFZ公債標售。這次寬鬆面對的是燃料與運輸成本惡化，而不是明確好轉的通膨環境。

## 馬來西亞籌得美元，能源支出改變主權融資需求

馬來西亞顯示，即使能源衝擊未退，需求穩健的借款人仍能以有利條件進入市場。五年來首次美元發行透過伊斯蘭債券（sukuk）募集$15億：2032年4月到期的$8.5億，殖利率4.612%；2036年7月到期的$6.5億，殖利率4.949%。認購倍數4.7倍，最終利差較初步指引收窄30個基點。

第2季GDP年增5.8%、優於預期，內需、半導體投資與電子出口提供支撐。募資用於專案及既有債務再融資，但政府也面對上升的燃料補貼支出。2026年汽柴油補貼可能達MYR400億，遠高於MYR150億預算。強勁成長有助吸引債券買盤，高油價若持續，財政仍會承受更大負擔。

波斯灣國家也在準備規模更大的基建支出。2026年區域發債已達紀錄$1,120億，沙烏地阿拉伯、科威特、阿聯酋與卡達考慮興建可繞過荷莫茲的港口、管線及道路。科威特近期完成的$60億發行，即使石油出口受阻，仍獲逾2倍訂單；巴林在開戰後不久也募集$10億。外匯準備與評等持續支撐融資，政府則增加了新的支出需求。

較強的發行人也無法避免成本上升。阿布達比2054年債券利差約美債加82個基點，1月為53個基點，衝突與預期供給壓抑債價。沙烏地、阿聯酋及阿曼，比科威特、巴林與卡達更有替代路線可用；但紅海攻擊也說明，繞開荷莫茲不等於消除航運風險。舉債興建新路線，有助保護未來收入，過程中卻會增加債務及市場供給。

美元計價主權債週五小幅回升。EMB漲0.12%，整週仍跌0.93%、一個月跌1.68%。美元指數大致持平於101.47，讓市場在美元單週升0.71%後稍獲喘息。美國實質殖利率與燃料成本仍高，外匯收入或補貼預算容易受長期運輸中斷影響的國家，壓力尤其沉重。

## 油價與波動率回落，晶片股跌勢未止

股市並未一致跟隨美債反彈。S&P 500幾乎持平，Nasdaq 100卻跌1.15%，費城半導體指數跌4.25%，一個月跌幅擴大至12.34%。油價下降減輕了大盤部分壓力，對AI投資回報的疑慮卻仍在，與科技借款人面對的利差擴大、訂單不足同時發生。

VIX下跌0.64%至18.58，美元指數單日僅升0.04%，黃金則漲0.52%至$4,067.60。油價回落帶來喘息，卻沒有消除地緣政治避險需求，也未恢復市場對科技支出的信心。相較幾乎不動的大盤指數，這些分歧更能說明當天變化：能源衝擊暫時緩和，AI融資的調整仍在持續。

## 聯準會與大型AI交易，揭開密集的一週

7月28至29日FOMC，將與第2季GDP、6月通膨數據一同成為下週焦點。市場預估GDP季增年率約2.1%，通膨放慢；官員還須把這些回顧性數據，與重新升高的能源風險及已生效關稅一起評估。7月維持利率仍較可能，但在升息機率約35%的情況下，聲明與記者會同樣重要。若實質殖利率開始下降，才會比週五僅靠通膨補償縮小的行情，更接近全面反彈。

Sopaipilla預計7月27日定價。最終條件與次級交易，將顯示約287.5個基點的指引，是否足以在1.6倍訂單下完成$123億發行。隨後Microsoft、Meta與Amazon支出更新，讓投資人再次比較融資需求與未來現金流。新券和既有長天期科技債的價格，將直接反映市場如何重估兩者。

7月30日英國央行、7月31日日本銀行，接續完成主要政策決策。英國投資人須把指引與5%以上殖利率、即將到來的縮表決定合併評估；日本則面對接近164兌$1的日圓與上升的超長債殖利率。即使兩家央行不動利率，當地市場反應也會改變美債相對吸引力。日圓回升、長天期日本公債反彈，與匯率續貶、國內殖利率再升，將帶來截然不同的海外配置環境。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
# Oil gives Treasuries a reprieve as AI debt strains demand

## A Friday rally leaves the week's bond losses largely intact

Treasuries recovered on Friday as oil slipped back below $100, but the relief stopped short of reversing a difficult week for bonds. The 2-year yield fell 4 basis points to 4.33% and the 10-year declined 2 to 4.69%. Both remained about 15 basis points above the previous Friday. At 5.16%, the 30-year yield barely moved despite Brent's 3.88% decline to $96.78.

The rally reduced inflation compensation, not the real cost of borrowing. The 10-year breakeven fell 2 basis points to 2.26%, while the real yield held at 2.43%. Stronger US services activity and new-home sales, newly effective import duties and uncertain Fed guidance kept a July rate increase in play. Markets still assigned it roughly 35% odds ahead of the July 28–29 meeting.

Corporate borrowers faced a different obstacle: buyers were struggling to absorb repeated large AI financings. A $12.3 billion bond sale for a Meta data center had attracted $20 billion of orders by late Friday, just 1.6 times the issue size, with pricing still expected on Monday. Barclays estimates also showed the largest technology borrowers contributing more duration-times-spread risk to the US high-grade market than the largest banks. Oil relief helped government bonds, but did little to resolve that growing supply burden or the pressure from competing sovereign yields in Britain and Japan.

## Lower oil eases the front end, while real yields hold firm

The Treasury rally followed three sessions of front-led losses. Five-year yields fell 3 basis points to 4.43%, between the 4-basis-point decline at two years and the 1-basis-point decline at 30 years. The curve steepened: 2s10s widened 2 basis points to 36 and 2s30s widened 3 to 83.

Oil offered the immediate respite. WTI fell 3.12% to $89.31 as tankers continued to move through Middle East routes and reports of mediation offered some hope of de-escalation. The shipping picture was far from normal. Houthi attacks had extended the threat from Hormuz toward the Red Sea, and some vessels were avoiding the route or moving without transponders. Brent was still 9.85% higher than a week earlier and 25.56% higher than a month earlier; WTI's weekly gain was 8.27%.

That left the week's rates adjustment largely in place. The 2- and 5-year yields each finished 15 basis points higher, the 10-year rose 14 and the 30-year 10. Monthly increases were 17, 16, 19 and 22 basis points, respectively. Friday's front-end recovery gave back only part of the latest policy repricing, while the long end continued to carry losses accumulated over the month.

Inflation-linked bonds made the limit of the rally particularly clear. The 10-year real yield was unchanged at 2.43%, up 12 basis points over the week and 14 over the month. The 2-basis-point fall in breakevens accounted for the entire nominal 10-year rally and left that inflation measure only 2 basis points higher for the week. Investors accepted a little less inflation compensation as oil eased without accepting a lower real yield.

The Fed's decision was still unusually open. July hike odds near 35% compared with roughly 10% after the cooler June CPI report; a hold remained the more likely outcome. Chairman Kevin Warsh's reduced reliance on forward guidance added uncertainty, and the MOVE Index reached its highest since May. Economists continued to expect the next Fed move to be a cut even as financial markets priced higher borrowing costs.

New US activity reports gave policymakers little reason to rush toward easing. Business activity expanded at its fastest pace in eight months as services offset cooler manufacturing, and new-home sales rose. Duties of 10%–12.5% on imports from about 60 economies also took effect, replacing an expiring 10% global import tax. The price impact would emerge over time, through some combination of higher consumer prices, lower margins and changes in trade. For now, the Fed had to assess another potential cost shock against demand that was still holding up.

Long bonds benefited least. The 20-year-plus Treasury index remained down 1.48% over the week and 4.39% over the month. Government borrowing and technology capital expenditure continued to draw on overlapping pools of long-duration capital. A 1-basis-point decline in the 30-year yield on a day of sharply lower oil showed how little of that pressure Friday's rally had removed.

## Meta's orderbook puts a price on the AI supply burden

The latest Meta-linked financing turned a general concern about AI borrowing into a concrete demand test. BlackRock's Sopaipilla Investor was marketing $12.3 billion of notes due in 2048 to fund a data-center campus in El Paso. Final orders reached $20 billion late Friday, according to people familiar with the sale. At 1.6 times the bonds offered, demand was well below the roughly four-times average for investment-grade deals this year. Pricing was expected on July 27, not completed at Friday's close.

Guidance around 287.5 basis points over 10-year Treasuries was roughly 40 basis points wider than a comparable Beignet note due in 2049. That existing Meta-linked security had itself widened more than 50 basis points during July. The new deal's payment structure offered support: a special-purpose vehicle gradually repays principal, backed by Meta's lease commitments, for a campus expected to deliver as much as 1 gigawatt of computing capacity. BlackRock subsidiaries Global Infrastructure Management and HPS Investment Partners own 80% of the project and Meta 20%.

Those protections had not produced an abundant orderbook. Amazon's $25 billion sale earlier in July also attracted just 1.6 times coverage. Meta's $25 billion April financing had priced wider than its $30 billion transaction six months earlier, and an April note due in 2046 had since widened 30 basis points. These earlier deals supplied a useful comparison for Sopaipilla: repeated large offerings were costing borrowers more even when the tenant or issuer remained highly rated.

Barclays' index analysis showed why the effects could reach beyond individual deals. As of July 23, the six largest technology companies accounted for 8.6% of US high-grade duration-times-spread exposure, above the six largest banks' 7.3%. Hyperscalers represented only about 4% of principal outstanding, versus roughly 9% for those banks, but their long maturities magnified their contribution. Of hyperscaler issuance in the past year, 43% matured beyond ten years, compared with 24% of M&A debt and 23% of other nonfinancial issuance.

Technology investment-grade spreads had risen to about 89 basis points from roughly 76 at the start of 2026. Barclays projected approximately $285 billion of global high-grade hyperscaler issuance this year. Existing holders therefore faced both interest-rate exposure and the risk that new supply would reset spreads on outstanding bonds. Broad credit funds were almost unchanged on Friday—LQD slipped 0.03%, HYG was flat and JNK fell 0.01%—but their calm daily performance obscured the longer adjustment. LQD had lost 2.46% over the month, versus 0.80% for HYG and 0.89% for JNK, with investment grade carrying the larger duration burden.

Away from AI, financing activity reflected more specific balance-sheet problems. Victoria reported an annual loss of £326.3 million after writedowns and debt-reduction costs. The loss underscored the operating burden behind its refinancing, which had moved forward earlier in the week after HSBC backed the contested restructuring of its 2028 notes.

Charter Communications sought to simplify and extend a complicated debt structure before maturities became more pressing. Its offers covered about $10 billion of affiliate and Time Warner Cable bonds and up to $9.7 billion of other subsidiary debt. Depending on participation, it could issue as much as $3.5 billion of new notes due in 2038 and 2041. Exchange terms, priority levels and participation caps meant the effects would differ by bondholder; the transaction was not a uniform reduction in debt.

Two stressed European borrowers were arranging liquidity while still repairing operations. Junk-rated South East Water secured a £200 million backstop for a future bond sale, supporting cash and a £1.9 billion investment plan. Gearing stood at 66.5% against a 55% target, and service failures had brought a £30.5 million redress package. BayWa's liabilities exceeded €10 billion after debt-funded expansion. An earlier restructuring had required about €1.3 billion of fresh bank debt; the next plan envisaged subordinating as much as €700 million of loans, at least €220 million of shareholder capital and asset sales.

The institutions supplying private capital were changing too. Private-equity investment in life insurers had grown from about $23 billion in 2009 to roughly $250 billion. Insurance capital rules based on ratings can give bespoke private structures more favorable charges than comparably risky public bonds. That expanding funding source made the quality of ratings and the ties between asset managers and insurers increasingly important alongside the underlying loans.

China's lenders were dealing with almost the opposite problem: weak demand and falling market rates. ICBC, China Merchants Bank and Shanghai Pudong Development Bank's Haikou branch issued initial loans linked to depository-institution repo rates rather than relying only on the loan prime rate. ICBC lent CNY76.7 million for one year at a rate linked to overnight repo; SPDB's loan was CNY7 million, while state media put China Merchants' at CNY8 million. Nearly half of loans issued in March were already priced below the LPR, up from 16% in 2019. Using traded funding rates offered a more responsive reference as the administered benchmark lagged the decline in interbank rates and bond yields.

## Global sovereign yields resist the US relief rally

Outside the US, investors still had to contend with sovereign yields at multiyear highs. The average yield on the Bloomberg Global Treasury Index reached 3.68%, the highest since 2008. German ten-year yields were at their highest since 2011, UK yields remained above 5%, and Japan's longest bonds fell further.

The UK ten-year yield declined about 4 basis points on Friday to around 5.04%, but had stayed above 5% throughout the week, its longest such stretch in almost two decades. Energy-import dependence and uncertainty over Prime Minister Andy Burnham's spending plans complicated the fiscal outlook. June debt-service costs of £11.8 billion showed the cost of carrying a large debt stock at higher rates.

The Bank of England's bond sales were another part of the supply calculation. It had to decide how quickly to reduce its remaining £492 billion gilt portfolio in the year starting in October. Sales of £21 billion, together with maturities, had produced an overall £70 billion reduction in the current quantitative-tightening year. Redemptions would fall sharply in the next year, just as the Debt Management Office planned more long-dated issuance. Earlier BOE analysis estimated that quantitative tightening had added 15–25 basis points to ten-year yields.

Euro-area surveys offered a softer inflation picture, but one that predated the latest oil surge. Consumer expectations for one year fell to 3% from 3.5%, and three-year expectations to 2.8% from 2.9%. Companies expected wage growth of 2.5% in 2026 and 2.4% in 2027, after 3.1% in 2025; selling-price increases were also less pronounced than anticipated. The consumer poll ran from June 4–29 and the corporate conversations ended July 1. Those results gave the ECB some reassurance about earlier price pressure, not a reading of how households and firms would respond to $100 oil.

After Thursday's hold, officials kept September tightening open. Euro-area private-sector activity also reached a five-month high, limiting the growth argument for restraint. Separately, the ECB began onboarding foreign central banks for an enhanced repo facility available from the fourth quarter of 2026 through the five largest national central banks. It extended climate factors to nonfinancial corporate credit claims used as collateral, seeking protection against transition-related valuation losses. The measures concerned access to euro liquidity and collateral treatment, rather than a change in the current policy rate.

Japan's currency and super-long debt remained under pressure together. The yen weakened to 163.99 per dollar, its lowest since November 1986, and the 40-year JGB yield rose 10 basis points to 4.01%, approaching May's 4.355% record. Higher import costs compounded uncertainty over funding for prospective tax cuts and defense spending.

The BOJ was widely expected to hold on July 31 after lifting its policy rate to 1% in June. Markets nevertheless priced about 32 basis points of tightening by year-end, while half of surveyed economists placed the next increase in December. Faster tightening could raise domestic yields and make foreign bonds less attractive; waiting risked further yen weakness and imported inflation. Either route left super-long investors with a difficult combination of currency, policy and fiscal uncertainty.

Fiscal strains were also visible in Belgium. Morningstar DBRS affirmed AA but changed the outlook to negative, with debt at 107.9% of GDP and the euro area's largest deficit, 5.2%, projected to reach 5.7% by 2028. The coalition sought €10 billion of consolidation through 2029. DBRS considered a larger adjustment unlikely under the existing political constraints.

Russia faced inflation pressure even as its central bank extended a yearlong easing cycle on Friday. Before the decision, the policy rate stood at 14.25%; seasonally adjusted annualized inflation had accelerated to 10.6% in June and household expectations to 14.7%. Gasoline was 20% more expensive than a year earlier, and the Finance Ministry had halted OFZ auctions amid weak bids. The easing came against worsening fuel and transport costs, rather than an unambiguously improving inflation outlook.

## Malaysia raises dollars as energy bills reshape sovereign funding

Malaysia showed that borrowers with strong demand could still secure favorable access despite the energy shock. Its first dollar sale in five years raised $1.5 billion through sukuk: $850 million due in April 2032 at 4.612% and $650 million due in July 2036 at 4.949%. Orders covered the deal 4.7 times, allowing spreads to tighten 30 basis points from initial guidance.

Second-quarter GDP growth of 5.8% from a year earlier beat expectations, supported by domestic demand, semiconductor investment and electronics exports. The government was borrowing to fund projects and refinance obligations, but also faced a rising fuel-subsidy bill. Petrol and diesel support could cost MYR40 billion in 2026 against a MYR15 billion budget allocation. Strong growth helped underpin demand for the bonds; prolonged expensive oil would still weaken the fiscal position.

Gulf borrowers were preparing for larger infrastructure bills of their own. Regional bond sales had reached a record $112 billion in 2026 as Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, the UAE and Qatar considered ports, pipelines and roads that bypass Hormuz. Kuwait's recently completed $6 billion issue had drawn more than twice that amount in bids despite disrupted oil exports, and Bahrain had raised $1 billion soon after the war began. Reserves and ratings continued to support access even as governments faced new spending needs.

The cost was rising even for stronger issuers. Abu Dhabi's 2054 bonds traded about 82 basis points over Treasuries, versus 53 in January, as conflict and prospective supply weighed on prices. Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Oman had better access to alternative routes than Kuwait, Bahrain and Qatar. Red Sea attacks nevertheless showed that moving traffic away from Hormuz did not remove shipping risk. Financing new routes could protect future revenues while adding debt and competing issuance in the meantime.

Hard-currency sovereign debt recovered modestly on Friday. EMB rose 0.12%, though it remained down 0.93% over the week and 1.68% over the month. The dollar index was nearly steady at 101.47, providing some respite after a 0.71% weekly rise. High US real yields and fuel costs continued to weigh most heavily on countries whose external earnings or subsidy budgets were vulnerable to a prolonged disruption.

## Chip losses persist even as oil and volatility retreat

The equity market did not share the Treasury rally evenly. The S&P 500 was almost unchanged, but the Nasdaq 100 fell 1.15% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index lost 4.25%, extending its monthly decline to 12.34%. Concern about returns on AI investment remained active even as lower oil relieved some pressure on the broader market. That weakness ran alongside the widening spreads and thin orderbooks confronting technology borrowers.

VIX eased 0.64% to 18.58. The dollar index rose just 0.04% on the day, while gold gained 0.52% to $4,067.60. Oil's decline thus brought a measure of relief without eliminating demand for geopolitical protection or restoring confidence in technology spending. The contrast was more informative than the almost flat headline equity index: the energy shock eased for a day, while the AI financing adjustment continued.

## The Fed and a large AI deal open a crowded week

The July 28–29 FOMC arrives alongside second-quarter GDP and June inflation data in the coming week. Forecasts put annualized growth near 2.1% and anticipated slower inflation. Policymakers must weigh those backward-looking releases against the renewed oil shock and effective tariffs. A hold is still the market's more likely July outcome, but its message matters with hike odds around 35%. For bondholders, a fall in real yields would mark a broader recovery than Friday's breakeven-led move.

Sopaipilla is expected to price on July 27. Final terms and subsequent trading will show whether guidance near 287.5 basis points is enough to place $12.3 billion with a 1.6-times orderbook. Microsoft, Meta and Amazon spending updates then give investors another chance to compare the financing pipeline with future cash generation. The new issue and existing long-dated technology bonds offer observable prices for that reassessment.

The BOE decision on July 30 and BOJ on July 31 complete the major policy sequence. UK investors will weigh guidance against yields above 5% and the coming runoff decision; Japan's face a yen near 164 per dollar and rising super-long yields. Moves in those markets will affect the relative appeal of Treasuries even if the central banks leave rates unchanged. A firmer yen and recovering long JGBs would offer a different backdrop from continued depreciation and another rise in domestic yields.
